summary: Validated decision-gated record for UuidSequenceNumber under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Executive. The clean Win25H2Clean baseline confirmed the live value, the residual static triage found an exact current-build ntoskrnl.exe Unicode hit, later KVM full-analysis replays confirmed that the string still exists but did not recover a direct or bounded indirect ntoskrnl code reference, the bounded Executive ETL review proved adjacent query and set activity for the same value during early boot, and later KVM local-KD follow-ups resolved both the live UUID symbol family and the current-build load/save path that opens a Session Manager Executive persisted-state location and queries or sets the `UuidSequenceNumber` value name. A deeper KVM local-KD value dump also showed live current-build in-memory UUID state on the working guest, and a later trigger-state follow-up wrapped the existing UUID / RPC / COM burst between two local-KD snapshots but still observed no delta: `ExpUuidSequenceNumber = 0x002caf1b`, `ExpUuidSequenceNumberValid = 1`, and `ExpUuidSequenceNumberNotSaved = 0` before and after the trigger. A subsequent API-level local-KD disassembly then showed that `ExUuidCreate` funnels into `ExpUuidGetValues`, `NtAllocateUuids` funnels into `ExpAllocateUuids`, and `ExpAllocateUuids` can update `ExpUuidSequenceNumber` and set `ExpUuidSequenceNumberNotSaved = 1` before `ExpUuidSaveSequenceNumberIf` runs. A direct user-mode API trigger built around repeated `UuidCreateSequential` plus `NtAllocateUuids` calls then also completed cleanly and still produced no state delta in the same local-KD snapshot lane. A follow-up seed and Config Manager disassembly then showed `NtSetUuidSeed` as a privileged seed-write path with `SeAccessCheck` and cache updates, while `CmpUuidCreate` turned out to be only a retry wrapper around `ExUuidCreate`. A later forced-invalid local-KD follow-up then cleared `ExpUuidSequenceNumberValid` to `0`, reran the same direct API burst, and observed `ExpUuidSequenceNumber` advance from `0x002caf1b` to `0x002caf1c` while `ExpUuidSequenceNumberValid` returned to `1` and `ExpUuidSequenceNumberNotSaved` stayed `0`. A later hardened-runner KVM Procmon replay then ensured an elevated guest shell, exported `240500` rows under the alternate Executive burst, and still returned zero `Session Manager\Executive` or `UuidSequenceNumber` hits. Runtime ETW and KVM Procmon lanes therefore still stay clean no-hits, but the lane now has a reproducible state-transition trigger once the live validity bit is cleared under local-KD, so the remaining gap is direct observation of the registry read rather than uncertainty about the current-build trigger surface.

validation_proof.notes: The Session Manager Executive baseline export and the 96-key phase-0 existence batch agree that UuidSequenceNumber exists on the clean Win25H2Clean baseline.

setting.name: Executive UUID Sequence Number
setting.casual_explanation: UuidSequenceNumber is a low-level Session Manager Executive value that appears to participate in early-boot UUID state handling.
setting.why_people_change_it: Researchers track it when studying Executive boot activity, UUID state handling, and adjacent low-level registry behavior under Session Manager Executive.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The lane now has baseline existence, an exact current-build ntoskrnl string hit, KVM full-analysis replays that still failed to recover a direct or bounded indirect ntoskrnl code reference, bounded early-boot ETL proof that the value is active in the same path, live KVM local-KD evidence that ties the current-build UUID load/save code path to a Session Manager Executive persisted-state location plus the exact `UuidSequenceNumber` value name, a live KVM local-KD value dump that confirms populated in-memory UUID state on the working guest, a later trigger-state follow-up that showed the existing UUID / RPC / COM burst does not move the observed UUID state variables, an API-level local-KD disassembly that identifies `ExUuidCreate` and `NtAllocateUuids` as the current-build allocation paths that sit on top of mutable sequence-state logic, a direct API trigger follow-up that still produced no state delta after repeated `UuidCreateSequential` and `NtAllocateUuids` calls, a seed/Config-Manager disassembly that classifies `NtSetUuidSeed` as a privileged write surface and `CmpUuidCreate` as an adjacent retry wrapper, a forced-invalid local-KD follow-up that turns the same direct API burst into a reproducible state-transition trigger by clearing `ExpUuidSequenceNumberValid`, and a hardened-runner KVM Procmon replay that still returned zero intended-path hits across a `240500`-row export. That is strong enough for a research-gated package, but not enough for Class A without a direct runtime read.
setting.professional_notes: Win25H2Clean exports confirm UuidSequenceNumber exists under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Executive with an observed baseline value of 0x1819f30 (25272112 decimal in the earlier baseline export and 25272111 in the later 96-key phase-0 live batch). Residual static triage then found an exact current-build Unicode string hit for UuidSequenceNumber in ntoskrnl.exe and no exact hit in smss.exe. A later KVM PDB-backed full-analysis replay confirmed the exact Unicode string at 140038cd8 in current-build ntoskrnl.exe, but still recovered zero direct references for that string in the analyzed program. A follow-up rerun with the updated bounded indirect string-reference search still recovered zero direct or bounded indirect references for that same string, which keeps the static lane at value-exists proof rather than a bounded code-path proof. A bounded host-side ETL review from the successful Session Manager Executive boot extract showed System (PID 4) querying and later setting UuidSequenceNumber during early boot, proving adjacent runtime activity in the intended path. A dedicated tools-hardened lightweight ETW follow-up on RegProbe-Baseline-ToolsHardened-20260330 then ran both short and split UUID / RPC / COM trigger profiles and still stayed a clean no-hit with exact_query_hits = 0 and path_line_count = 0. A later KVM Procmon replay on the working `regprobe-win11-25h2-session` guest reused the UUID / RPC / COM trigger family, exported 286763 Procmon rows, and still found zero `Session Manager\Executive` or `UuidSequenceNumber` hits. That KVM runtime pass also observed a live registry-side value of 2928393 on the working guest, so it strengthens the runtime no-hit story without replacing the earlier clean-baseline exports. The alternate Executive-burst follow-up also now completes cleanly on KVM instead of stalling as it did on the earlier VMware thread-burst attempt, but it still exported 273477 rows with zero `Session Manager\Executive`, `UuidSequenceNumber`, `AdditionalCriticalWorkerThreads`, or `AdditionalDelayedWorkerThreads` hits. A later hardened-runner replay then ensured an elevated guest shell automatically, reran that same Executive burst end to end, exported 240500 rows, and still returned zero `Session Manager\Executive`, `UuidSequenceNumber`, `AdditionalCriticalWorkerThreads`, or `AdditionalDelayedWorkerThreads` hits while the working guest reported a live registry-side value of 2928397 before and after restore. Supporting ReactOS source review had placed UuidSequenceNumber under the Rpc path, but newer current-build KVM local-KD evidence is stronger: a wildcard follow-up resolved `ExpUuidLoadSequenceNumber`, `ExpUuidSaveSequenceNumber`, `ExpUuidSaveSequenceNumberIf`, `ExpUuidSequenceNumber`, `ExpUuidSequenceNumberValid`, `ExpUuidSequenceNumberNotSaved`, and `ExpUuidSequenceNumberRegName` in the live guest kernel. A later disassembly and string-dump follow-up then showed `ExpUuidLoadSequenceNumber` calling `RtlGetPersistedStateLocation`, `RtlInitUnicodeString`, `ZwOpenKey`, and `ZwQueryValueKey`, with `ExpUuidSaveSequenceNumber` following the matching `ZwSetValueKey` path, while `ExpUuidSaveSequenceNumberIf` gates on `ExpUuidSequenceNumberNotSaved`. The same live debugger run resolved the path-builder strings to `\Registry\Machine\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Executive` and `KernelExecutive`, and resolved the `ExpUuidSequenceNumberRegName` buffer itself to `UuidSequenceNumber`. A later live KVM local-KD value dump then read `ExpUuidSequenceNumber = 0x002caf0c` (2928396 decimal), `ExpUuidSequenceNumberValid = 1`, and `ExpUuidSequenceNumberNotSaved = 0`. That in-memory value is only +3 above the earlier registry-side sample from the same working guest, which is consistent with active UUID state rather than a stale constant, but it still does not count as a simultaneous direct registry-read proof. A later trigger-state follow-up then wrapped the existing `uuid-rpc-com-burst` profile around two snapshots in the same attached debugger session. The helper executed successfully with trigger exit code 0, but `ExpUuidSequenceNumber` stayed `0x002caf1b` (2928411 decimal) before and after the burst while `ExpUuidSequenceNumberValid` remained `1` and `ExpUuidSequenceNumberNotSaved` remained `0`. That suggests the current UUID / RPC / COM burst is not materially mutating the persisted UUID state that the local-KD lane can observe on the working guest, so it does not currently look like a winning transport for a direct runtime-read proof. A subsequent API-level local-KD disassembly then clarified the more promising trigger family: `ExUuidCreate` routes through `ExpUuidGetValues` and later `ExpUuidSaveSequenceNumberIf`, while `NtAllocateUuids` routes through `ExpAllocateUuids` and then `ExpUuidSaveSequenceNumberIf`. Inside `ExpAllocateUuids`, the current build can call `ExpUuidLoadSequenceNumber` when the state is invalid, write back `ExpUuidSequenceNumber`, set `ExpUuidSequenceNumberValid = 1`, set `ExpUuidSequenceNumberNotSaved = 1`, and on the rollback branch even `inc dword ptr [nt!ExpUuidSequenceNumber]`. A final direct user-mode allocation burst then exercised repeated `UuidCreateSequential` and `NtAllocateUuids` calls from guest PowerShell with clean trigger exit code 0 and empty trigger stderr, but the local-KD snapshots still showed `ExpUuidSequenceNumber = 0x002caf1b`, `ExpUuidSequenceNumberValid = 1`, and `ExpUuidSequenceNumberNotSaved = 0` both before and after the burst. That means the obvious current-build user-mode allocation APIs are still no-delta while the live UUID cache is already valid. A later seed and Config Manager follow-up then narrowed the adjacent paths further: `NtSetUuidSeed` resolved as a privileged setter that builds SID and ACL state, runs `SeAccessCheck`, updates `ExpUuidCachedValues`, and marks `ExpUuidCacheValid`, while `ZwSetUuidSeed` was only the syscall stub and `CmpUuidCreate` resolved as a simple wrapper that calls `ExUuidCreate`, retries on `0xC000022D`, and does not expose a separate persisted-state reader. A subsequent forced-invalid local-KD follow-up then cleared `ExpUuidSequenceNumberValid` to `0` before rerunning the same direct API burst. In that run, the working guest advanced `ExpUuidSequenceNumber` from `0x002caf1b` to `0x002caf1c`, restored `ExpUuidSequenceNumberValid` from `0` back to `1`, and left `ExpUuidSequenceNumberNotSaved = 0`, which shows that the direct API family becomes a real state-transition trigger once the live cache is invalidated first. The remaining blocker is now exact runtime observation of the registry read on the working guest rather than uncertainty about the current-build code path or whether the user-mode trigger can drive the state machine at all.

decision.why: UuidSequenceNumber is backed by clean baseline existence, an exact current-build ntoskrnl string hit, KVM full-analysis replays that still did not recover a direct or bounded indirect ntoskrnl code reference, bounded early-boot ETL evidence that the same value is active under Session Manager Executive, a live KVM local-KD wildcard that resolves the current-build UUID load/save/state symbol family in the running guest, a deeper local-KD disassembly that ties the current-build code path to a Session Manager Executive persisted-state location plus the exact `UuidSequenceNumber` value name, and live local-KD value snapshots that show populated current-build UUID state with `Valid = 1` and `NotSaved = 0` on the working guest. A later trigger-state follow-up showed that the existing UUID / RPC / COM burst does not move those observed state variables, a subsequent API-level local-KD disassembly showed that `ExUuidCreate` and `NtAllocateUuids` are the current-build allocation paths that sit directly on top of the mutable UUID sequence-state machinery, a direct API burst built from those same user-mode allocation calls still produced no state delta while the cache stayed valid, a seed / Config Manager follow-up showed that `NtSetUuidSeed` and `CmpUuidCreate` are adjacent non-winning surfaces rather than the missing reader proof, and a forced-invalid local-KD follow-up then showed that the same direct API burst does become a winning state-transition trigger once `ExpUuidSequenceNumberValid` is cleared first. Multiple runtime lanes still stayed clean no-hits across both ETW and KVM Procmon transport shapes, including a hardened-runner KVM Executive-burst replay that ensured an elevated guest shell automatically and still surfaced zero intended-path hits. That is enough for a strong research package, but not enough for Class A until the live runtime read is observed directly.
